summary: Markdown gets the progressive disclosure Serena gives code: jarvis spec toc/section/search, a default-off PreToolUse refusal of whole-file spec dumps, prose that points agents at the commands instead of the file, and counters that measure the result.

children.title: Count doc reads and whole-file reads, and classify a doc dump
children.description: Lands first and owns the two classifiers a sibling consumes, so there is exactly one body. Your files: `navigation.py`, `nav_volume.py`, `cli._print_navigation`. Do NOT touch `hooks.py` — you add the classifiers, another child calls them from a refusal. Do not create `spec_index.py`, do not edit `dispatch.py`, `worker_brief.py` or `cli.py`'s subparsers, add no dashboard route, and create no catalog key. Done when `uv run pytest tests/test_navigation.py tests/test_nav_volume.py tests/test_inspection.py tests/test_autopsy.py -q` is green with every existing test in them unmodified.
children.acceptance: jarvis navigation --project jarvis_os --days 36500 and its --json print the new figures alongside, not instead of, the existing ones, and the payload carries both BEFORE_NOTE and DOC_BEFORE_NOTE. AND dumps_doc owns the range: with no limit_lines it is True for a ranged sed of a .md (counters count every dump) and False at limit_lines=200, and _dump_span returns 41 / 40 / None for sed -n '40,80p' / head -40 / cat.

children.title: jarvis spec toc, section and search
children.description: Your files: new `src/jarvis/spec_index.py`, new `tests/test_spec_index.py`, plus `ops.py` payload functions and a `cli.py` subparser. `jarvis fo spec <fo-id>` already exists and prints a FEATURE ORDER's spec — leave it, `ops.feature_spec` and the dashboard spec page alone. Do not touch `sections.py` (re-use only), `navigation.py`, `nav_volume.py`, `hooks.py`, `dispatch.py`, `worker_brief.py` or `concision.py`, and create no catalog key. Two siblings quote your three command strings verbatim — one in worker prose, one in a refusal — so the spellings in 4.3 are a contract you may not vary.
children.acceptance: spec_index.section equals sections.extract_section over all four cases of the table (number that resolves, number that resolves to nothing, name as a case-insensitive substring, nested heading included while the next same-level one is not); toc is asserted over BOTH the tidy fixture and this spec file, so the numbered sections and the unnumbered appendix are both exercised; every search hit carries the exact runnable jarvis spec section <path> <ref> command; a path outside the project root exits non-zero naming the root, asserted with a symlink out of the tree and not a ../ string. Then as a regression pin only: jarvis spec --help and jarvis fo spec --help both exit 0 and tests/test_feature_orders.py, tests/test_spec_page.py and tests/test_search.py stay green.

children.title: Refuse a whole-file read of a spec, default off
children.description: `navigation.is_spec_path` and `navigation.dumps_doc` are already on your branch — CALL them, never re-spell them, and edit neither `navigation.py` nor any counter in `nav_volume.py`. In `dispatch.py` your edit is the env block beside JARVIS_PY_NAV_HOOK at line 215 and nothing else: another child owns the spec prose at lines 456-467 and will conflict if you stray. Do not touch `spec_index.py`, `cli.py`, `worker_brief.py` or `concision.py`. Nothing ships on, so merging this changes no running worker's behaviour and the paired on/off assertion is the whole of your proof.
children.acceptance: New tests/test_doc_nav_hook.py, modelled on tests/test_py_nav_hook.py, with every reachability assertion made through hooks.preflight_decision rather than through the decision function. AND: the read limit resolves from the catalog, not from a module constant — worker.doc_read_limit_lines gets the same seven wiring rows as worker.doc_nav_hook, and a project setting it to a value other than 200 flips a borderline Read's verdict. The .py arm has NO threshold and grows none: a Read with no limit is refused, the same Read with limit=4000 passes. AND the SAME resolved bar governs both doc arms: section 5.4's matrix is seven inputs by two switch states, with sed -n '40,80p' and head -40 of a spec PASSING beside the sed -n '1,2000p' deny. A blanket Bash refusal fails this child. AND the malformed-env table: the limit env var set to abc, empty, 0, -5 or absent all resolve to the 200 fallback and none raises, asserted through preflight_decision.

children.title: Stop telling agents to read the whole spec
children.description: Three files: `dispatch.py` at lines 456-467 plus `_planner_prompt` and `_common_briefing`; `worker_brief.navigation_core`; `concision.subagent_context`. In `dispatch.py` do NOT touch the env block at line 215 — another child owns it and will conflict. Do not edit `navigation.py`, `nav_volume.py`, `hooks.py`, `spec_index.py` or `cli.py`, and flip no catalog key. Check first that `jarvis spec --help` exits 0 on your branch: the commands you name are built by a sibling, and prose naming a command that does not exist points every feature child at an error.
children.acceptance: The three command strings you write are byte-identical to section 4.3's, and the two tests asserting subagent_context({}) equals house_style() are rewritten to assert containment rather than deleted.

children.title: Prove a child navigates the spec instead of dumping it
children.description: Work in `evals/llm/`, extending the existing test_navigation_judgment.py harness, plus one identity assertion added to tests/test_navigation.py. You are the only child that observes the other three working together, and if you find a defect in one of their files you REPORT it rather than patching it: `hooks.py`, `navigation.py`, `spec_index.py`, `dispatch.py`, `worker_brief.py` and `concision.py` are all someone else's. Do not flip worker.doc_nav_hook in the catalog or in dispatch — set the env var in the eval's own settings file. Do not shrink the existing arm matrix or re-grade the .py side.
children.acceptance: The canary token and the jarvis-spec-call assertion both hold on the hook-on arm; the hook-off arm is recorded with xfail(strict=False); and the jarvis-on-PATH precondition fails the eval rather than skipping it.
